title: Ningxiang pig-derived Enterococcus hirae protects against E. coli-induced gut dysbiosis and inflammation via acetate/propionate-MyD88-NF-kappaB axis in piglets.
authors: Zhang, Longlin; Wu, Zichen; Shen, Haibo; Meng, Yunlong; Li, Hongkun; Cai, Rong; Tang, Dalin; Kang, Meng; Yin, Yulong; Tan, Bie; Wang, Jing
one_liner_zh: 该文研究益生菌通过代谢物调控肠道炎症信号通路，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Intestinal inflammation, often driven by microbial dysbiosis and infections, remains a significant health challenge with limited effective treatments. Identifying probiotic strains with anti-inflammatory properties and elucidating their mechanisms is essential for developing novel therapeutic strategies. This study investigates the molecular mechanisms by which E. hirae-a lactic acid bacterium (LAB) isolated from Ningxiang piglets with low diarrhea incidence-alleviates E. coli-induced intestinal inflammation. RESULTS: In the present study, comparative analysis showed that Ningxiang piglets exhibited a significantly lower incidence of diarrhea and reduced E. coli abundance compared to Yorkshire piglets. Notably, E. hirae was more abundant in Ningxiang piglets and correlated with elevated secretory IgA levels. Additionally, in vitro antagonism assays found that E. hirae effectively inhibited E. coli growth. In vivo supplementation of E. hirae in E. coli-infected piglets restored intestinal microbial balance, increased levels of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) such as acetate and propionate, and mitigated E. coli colonization. Further analyses suggested that acetate and propionate downregulated the MyD88/NF-kappaB signaling pathway, thereby reducing pro-inflammatory cytokine expression. Molecular docking and MyD88 (- / - )experiments verified that MyD88 is involved in SCFA-mediated protection against E. coli-induced inflammation. Furthermore, analyses of public human datasets revealed that Crohn's disease patients exhibited a similar reduction in SCFA levels and MyD88-NF-kappaB pathway activation, suggesting potential clinical relevance. CONCLUSION: Token together, our results reveal that Ningxiang pig-derived E. hirae alleviates E. coli-induced gut dysbiosis and inflammation potentially through the acetate/propionate-MyD88-NF-kappaB axis. This work provides mechanistic insights for further exploration of probiotic and postbiotic approaches against bacterial-induced intestinal inflammation. Video Abstract.
abstract_zh: 背景：肠道炎症通常由微生物失调和感染驱动，仍是重大健康挑战，且有效治疗方法有限。识别具有抗炎特性的益生菌菌株并阐明其机制，对于开发新型治疗策略至关重要。本研究探讨了从腹泻发生率低的宁乡仔猪中分离出的乳酸菌（LAB）E. hirae缓解大肠杆菌诱导的肠道炎症的分子机制。结果：在本研究中，比较分析显示，与约克夏仔猪相比，宁乡仔猪的腹泻发生率显著降低，大肠杆菌丰度减少。值得注意的是，E. hirae在宁乡仔猪中更为丰富，并与分泌型IgA水平升高相关。此外，体外拮抗实验发现，E. hirae有效抑制大肠杆菌生长。在感染大肠杆菌的仔猪中补充E. hirae，恢复了肠道微生物平衡，增加了短链脂肪酸（SCFAs）如乙酸和丙酸的水平，并减轻了大肠杆菌的定植。进一步分析表明，乙酸和丙酸下调了MyD88/NF-kappaB信号通路，从而减少了促炎细胞因子的表达。分子对接和MyD88（-/-）实验验证了MyD88参与SCFA介导的对抗大肠杆菌诱导炎症的保护作用。此外，对公共人类数据集的分析显示，克罗恩病患者表现出类似的SCFA水平降低和MyD88-NF-kappaB通路激活，提示潜在的临床相关性。结论：总体而言，我们的结果表明，源自宁乡猪的E. hirae可能通过乙酸/丙酸-MyD88-NF-kappaB轴缓解大肠杆菌诱导的肠道失调和炎症。这项工作为进一步探索益生菌和后生元方法对抗细菌诱导的肠道炎症提供了机制见解。视频摘要。
